Commentary.Commentary: 429.2 overs, 1533 runs, 24 wickets - the relevant numbers for the game. Sums up the match, right? Test cricket certainly doesn't require such games for its advancements. With a hope that the following game doesn't offer the same, we head to Dhaka for the second Test. It begins on the 8th of February, 2018 from 0930 local time (0330 GMT). Do join us. Till then, take care. Cheers! Adios! Meanwhile, you can catch some limited overs action by switching to the ongoing South Africa vs India game.

Mominul Haque became the first cricketer from Bangladesh to score two tons in a single Test. He also returned with most runs in a game for a player of his nation - 281. His love affair with Chittagong continued. Rightly so, he is adjudged the MAN OF THE MATCH.

In reply, Sri Lanka turned up with a mountain of runs as the each from the second wicket to the sixth wicket stand crossed the 50-run mark. The 308-run association between Kusal Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva helped them build a strong reply. Both of them got daddy hundreds but missed out on double tons. Even Roshen Silva used up the chance to get to his maiden test ton. Taijul Islam and Mehidy Hasan picked up 7 wickets between them. With a 200-run lead, the visitors came out all guns blazing but then an effective response from Haque and Das turned out to be their undoing.

Earlier in the game, the hosts had no hesitation in batting first. The 236-run partnership between Mominul Haque and Mushfiqur Rahim helped them set the base for a big score. The hometown southpaw stroked his way to a huge score while the latter missed out on his ton by 8 runs. Even Tamim Iqbal and Mahmudullah used the occasion to add a half century to their kitty. For the Lankans, Suranga Lakmal and Rangana Herath turned up with three apiece.

Here is what Liton Das has got to say when he is caught up after the game. He says that he thought of reaching his landmark in style quickly and hence came down the track to that ball and played the shot. Athar Ali Khan takes the mike from him and states that the youngster has realised his mistake. On being asked about his stand with Mominul Haque, the wicketkeeper-batsman states that he and the southpaw decided to take it over by over and that worked. He opines that the middle of the track was very flat and the areas outside the stumps had some roughs.

After the two batters departed in succession, the tourists sensed an opening to get a positive result in their favour. But Mahmudullah and Mosaddek Hossain combined together for a stand worth 28 that took 106 balls, which signified that the game was moving nowhere and only one outcome looked assured, which is what happened.

Such has been the nature of the track, that wonder if it is right to give credit to Bangladesh for this or whether to blame the placid pitch for the tame run-filled boring draw. The hosts came into the final day still 119 adrift of Sri Lanka's total. They had lost three quick wickets towards the end of Day 4, to stare at a possible innings defeat. But Mominul Haque and Liton Das had different plans. They stitched together a 180-run stand and quelled any hopes that the visitors would have had of an early end to the game. The southpaw passed the triple figure mark for the 6th time in Tests, 5th in Chittagong, while the latter missed out on his by a mere 6 runs.

That's that! The SHAKE OF HANDS THAT WE ALL AWAITED! It's come. Both the sides decide that it isn't possible to eke out a result from this point and decide to settle for a DRAW. Wonder who will the happier of the two sides at the end of the game.

Welcome back! We're all set for the final segment of this game. Mahmudullah will face Rangana Herath to begin proceedings. Here we go...
... Final Day, Final Session ...

So, we've got a match in our hands here. 81 runs ahead with 5 wickets in hand, can't really say who's ahead at the moment. We have 31 overs more to be bowled, with a possible two overs reduction due to the change of innings. Will this game go down to the wire? Will be in a position to start the talks of 5-dat Test cricket at its best et al? Let's see. See ya soon!

The session began in a sedate way but Mominul and Liton got about to scoring runs at a fast pace. So much so that, they took some risks, getting dropped in the process. Eventually Mushfiqur Rahim signaled to them from their dressing room to calm down. That they did, as both of them strung together a 180-run stand. At this point, because of the pair, they lead by 81. Rangana Herath and Dilruwan Perera have bowled their hearts out while Dhananjaya de Silva turned out to be the one with the golden arm. Lakshan Sandakan was all but disciplined and frugal.

A happening session! In fact the last hour, we can say. 46/2 in the 14 overs after the drinks interval. Sri Lanka certainly had some magic potion then or maybe a lucky one as they prised out the two set batters after that. Mominul Haque got a very good delivery that he had to play. More than that, the catch by Dimuth Karunaratne was to be credited. Then, a certain youngster aged 35, going around with the name of Dilruwan Perera took a well-judged stunner to end Liton Das' stay. The batter had to be blamed first because he threw away a golden opportunity to get to a triple figures.
Perera bowls this from round the wicket and lands it around middle and leg. Hossain lunges and defends this one solidly to walk unbeaten into TEA, FINAL DAY!

Another slip added.

Maiden. Mahmudullah blocks this one with a prod.

However, there was a sound as the ball passed the bat. Yet, nobody among the players really appeal. Karunaratne seems to have heard something and he urges his skipper to go for the DRS. Chandimal obliges, even as Mosaddek signals to his partner that he hasn't hit it. Snicko confirms the same and Sri Lanka lose a review.
Review time! Things really happening here now. There is a caught behind appeal against Hossain that is taken upstairs by Sri Lanka. There seems to be some noise but no real elation from the players.

OUT! DILRUWAN TAKES A STUNNER! What a catch to send the set Das back! It is a poor shot to be frank. Herath floats it up around off, Liton gets down the track and looks to get to his milestone with a glory shot. He fails to get to the pitch of the ball and due to the little spin on the ball, he ends up skying it high in the air. Perera sidetracks from mid off and goes towards long off. Never did he take his eyes off the ball. In the end, he turned around and takes that catch with a dive. The entire Sri Lanka side comes to him to congratulate him as he sits there in disbelief. Remember, he is 35 years young! Inexplicable shot from the Bangladesh keeper this. He walks back 6 runs short of his MAIDEN Test ton.

FOUR! Dropped! Lakshan Sandakan the man. Floated on the stumps, Mahmudullah gets down and sweeps it aerially towards deep mid-wicket. Sandakan there runs to his left, gets to the ball but fails to hang on to that. What's more, the ball goes through his hands and into the fence.
Das gets to the other end with a drive through mid on.

FOUR! Lovely shot. Loopy ball outside off, Das gets to the pitch of the ball with a stride forward and drives it through covers. The ball speeds away to the fence. The lead is now three quarters of a century. Liton moves into the 90s now.

A mini-conference in the middle. Herath, Chandimal and Lakmal stand at de Silva's bowling mark and have some thoughts exchanged. Dhananjaya will continue.

Could have been fatal! Mahmudullah pushes it towards covers and races down for a run. However, his partner didn't move an inch, seeing the fielder rush to the ball. However, Sandakan, the man there, failed to collect the ball in a go and return the throw and the home side skipper gets back in safely.

OUT! The magnum opus Test match with the bat ends for Mominul Haque! Gets an almost unplayable delivery for his downfall. De Silva loops it up nicely outside off, the angle is such that the southpaw has to play that. Mominul lunges and defends but the ball turns away just a touch to grab the outside edge. Now for the other part of this dismissal. The ball passes close past the keeper's gloves. Karunaratne is alert at first slip and swoops quickly to his right and takes that with a dive. Terrific catch that. The visitors leap up in celebration as they know the value of this scalp. Take a bow, Haque. What a game he has played! Top class. He walked in when his side were 148 runs behind, walks out with his side 61 ahead.

HISTORY CREATED! 6th Test ton for Mominul Haque, his SECOND IN THIS GAME. He becomes the first from his nation to achieve this feat. He knows the magnitude of the achievement and leaps up, punching his fists as he gets to the other end. The Bangladesh players rush out to the balcony to applaud and cheer their savior in the game. Remember, they were precariously placed last evening and he has been in the thick of the things for them to be in the position that they are in now. How does he get to the mark? Taps the loopy ball towards covers and hares to the other end. Well played, young man. Chittagong Hero for sure. That places the hosts 37 runs in front.
Flatter and outside off, cut away but straight to the man at point.
Mominul on strike. 99 reads his score.

A huge appeal put up by Lahiru, turned down. The action's not over. Haque was down the track in search of a run to get back on strike. As the ball had rolled towards backward point, the slip fielder gets there and fires a throw at the non-striker's end. It missed the stumps but Mominul had made it in. Careful, boy.
Lahiru Kumara back on now.

This is not good. Lahiru Kumara is not looking comfortable at all and has called for the physio. In fact, KUMARA IS GOING OFF THE FIELD. Definitely not good news for Sri Lanka, with the second Test starting in 3 days' time. Danushka Gunathilaka comes in as the substitute. Meanwhile, Mushfiqur Rahim comes out from the dressing room and asks the batsmen to calm down a bit. Rightly so. Too many shots being played too early. Bangladesh are not out of the woods yet.

Goes back and works it towards mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, Mominul reaches out and smothers the spin.
Outside off, spinning in a long way, LD looks to tuck it away but wears it on the pads. The ball lobs in the air but wide of any human being.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, Liton reaches out and looks to drive but gets an inside edge back to the bowler.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.

FOUR! You will get that with chinaman bowlers. A full toss here and there and Liton Das does not miss out. He reaches out and drives it through the covers for a boundary! His third Fifty in Tests, probably his most important one.
Down the leg side, spinning way down too, left alone.
Lakshan Sandakan to bowl from the other end.
The batsman works it down the leg side.

DROPPED! Oh dear... have Sri Lanka missed an opportunity there? Replays do indicate that. Landed outside off, Mominul goes back, aiming to steer the ball behind point but gets a bottom edge which goes towards the keeper. However, Niroshan Dickwella cannot gather it, probably because the ball came quickly off the bottom edge. Big moment.
Another easy single. Liton eases this through the covers.
Landed outside off, Das comes forward and pushes it back to the bowler.
Pushes this through mid on for a single. Ticking them off...
Full and outside off, pushed towards point.
Welcome back. 62 overs left in the day. This hour should decide the fate of this match. Rangana Herath vs Mominul Haque first up. Here we go...
... DAY 5, SECOND SESSION ...

So? What do you reckon? When you would have had a balance at the start of the day, kept a draw on one side and a Lankan win on the other, the latter would have been heavier. Now, the game is exactly balanced. Couple of quick wickets after Lunch and Sri Lanka would smell a win. On the other hand, another wicketless hour and we could still see the series as 0-0 when the second Test begins on the 8th of this month. Join us back at 1210 local (0610 GMT).

Nothing much happening for Sri Lanka. When they picked up 3 wickets last evening, their hopes would have gone up but it just seems that the purchase available on Day 4 has disappeared on Day 5. However, a bit bizarre captaincy from Dinesh Chandimal as he was okay with giving singles away. Might as well have kept the field attacking and encouraged the batsmen to improvise. That would not have guaranteed wickets but at least the scoreboard would not have been ticking. Who knows - Liton could have tried a couple of fancy shots and even gifted his wicket away. Defensive captaincy.

Mominul Haque, well, he has been magnificent. No Bangladeshi batsman has ever scored two tons in a Test match and the southpaw is just 30 runs adrift from creating that record. Calm and composed with a wagonwheel which shows runs scored all around the ground, except the third man region, where he has got only 3. Which means that he has avoided the dab shot or the run down shot. Excellent discipline.

Given that two of Bangladesh's heavy run-getters were dismissed yesterday itself, one would have expected the home side to fold up quickly this morning. But while Mominul has continued to enjoy his romance with Chittagong, the biggest positive for Bangladesh has been the batting of Liton Das. The latter normally bats in a bit rash manner but today he has understood the situation and mixed caution with aggression. He has faced 89 balls which is nearly more than an hour of overs bowled.
A wonderful session for the home side! 28.1 overs, 106 runs and no wicket! Not many expected this but the pair of Mominul Haque and Liton Das have quelled all alarms or thoughts.

And the session is seen off with ease. A bit of a drama on the final ball as Dhananjaya pushes it fuller and in response, Haque pushes forward. But he does so with hard hands and as a result, the ball scoots off the inside edge but wide of short leg. A single to go into the break. LUNCH ON DAY 5, BANGLADESH TRAIL BY 13 RUNS!
Full and around off, pushed straight to cover.
This time he does not miss out. Another long hop, pulled through fine leg for a couple.
A short ball down the leg side, Mominul looks to pull but misses. That ball hurried onto him and went off his pads wide of short leg.
Outside leg, watchfully kept down.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They manage to come back for the second.
Interesting. Dhananjaya de Silva to bowl the final over before Lunch.
A proper arm ball, pushed towards mid off.
Full and a bit faster than the previous one, straight as an arrow though, Liton is forward to block.
Action replay of the previous ball.
Very full and straight, blocked towards the bowler.
Full and outside off, eased straight to cover.
Full on leg stump, just a little bit of drift, Das lunges and works it towards short leg.
Rangana Herath is back on. Mostly he will bowl only one over before Lunch.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! 100-RUN STAND IS UP! Well played, lads. Kept Sri Lanka at bay. Full and around leg stump, Mominul gets down and looks to sweep. Gets a bit of a top edge but it sails well over Lahiru Kumara at short fine leg. The Sri Lankans cry in ecstasy, which later turns into agony as they realize that it would have needed two Lahiru Kumaras standing on top of one another to take that catch.

LBW appeal but the ball is pitching outside leg. Haque stretches to defend but misses and is pinged on the pads. There is some confusion between our scorers whether there was an inside edge or not and from the first replay, it seemed to have missed the edge. However, another replay seemed to indicate that the ball hit the pad, then the bat and went towards silly point. Not quite sure.
On middle, Mominul goes back and works it to the leg side.
NO BALL! Third no ball from Dilruwan, all in this spell itself. Outside off, Liton gets out another reverse sweep and earns a single through point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! The reverse sweeps are getting too frequent now. Outside off, Das gets down in a flash and spanks it behind point, towards the third man fence.

A conference going on in the middle. Everybody was there from Dickwella, Chandimal, Karunaratne, Herath, etc... surrounding the bowler. Was it just a huddle or some advice, can't say. If it was the latter, then there is a proverb which goes 'Too many cooks spoil the broth.' If it was just a huddle, then there are just 10 minutes to Lunch! Feel like it was a tactic from Chandimal, just to irritate the batsman. If I were a Bangladesh batsman, I would just love to waste as much time as possible. Thank you, Sri Lanka. I have to bat one over less now.
A bouncer, around off, coming in, Mominul ducks.
Outside off, on a length, pushed towards point for another easy single.
A full toss, Das is surprised as he just jabs it to cover.
On middle and leg, clipped straight to short mid-wicket.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, on a length, Das comes forward in a walk and blocks the ball to cover.

Really nice to see Roshan Abeysinghe taking note of all the stats. Especially where Sri Lanka are involved. Today Sri Lanka are celebrating their 70th Independence Day. Roshan gives us a stat that only Pakistan have won a match on their Independence Day. He is now busy checking whether any other team has done it or can Sri Lanka become the second nation. Well, the two men batting in the middle, will hope to bat for one more hour post Lunch to just take a Lankan win out of the window.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total. The deficit is down to 29. The stand is worth 90.
Full on middle, pushed through deepish mid on for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
There comes the reverse sweep, Das plays it through point for a single.
Fuller and outside off, solidly defended.
On middle and leg, played straight to short leg.
Pushes this through the covers for one more.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Down the leg side, tucked through fine leg for a run. Moves to 60.
Outside off again, punched through the covers again where Dhananjaya de Silva dives to his left to make a partial stop.
Outside off, an easy tap and run through point for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to mid off.

WIDE. That might seem like a poor ball from Kumara but one cannot blame the bowler here. In fact, it is a smart ploy. In his previous over, he banged a couple of balls around  the good length and short areas, which made the ball skid low. So considering that he bowled short here, it is not wrong. However, this one goes way over Das' head.
The arm ball, a touch short, MH is on guard as he punches it towards point.
Full and outside off, slowly tossed up, Haque gets a big stride forward and pushes the ball to cover.
Oho... the reverse sweep comes out now. Straight to Rangana Herath at deep backward point for a run.
Beaten. Few and far between though, for SDri lanka. Full and outside off, Das stretches to defend, expecting the ball to turn but it goes straight through and beats the outside edge.
Similar ball, same shot, but this one is much squarer, so Rangana Herath gets to the ball quickly. Just a single.
On middle and leg, worked through fine leg for a couple. The deficit is down to 38 now. The partnership is worth 81.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.

LBW??? No. BBW. The pitch indeed is playing tricks now. Kumara bangs it on a length outside off and Das goes back to defend. But the ball hits something and scoots low. Liton is pinged on the pads and Lahiru is up in an appeal but the wood comes in the way. Inside edge has saved Das.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

A short ball, Haque shows that he is not fazed from what happened on the previous ball as he pulls this comfortably through mid-wicket for a single. Okay... a milestone for Mr. Haque as he now registers the record for most runs in a Test match by a Bangladesh batsman. The previous record was held by Tamim Iqbal when he made 25 and 206 against Pakistan in Khulna in 2015. The Bangladeshi Bradman is back!

The physio is out in the middle. Looks alright, does Mominul, a bit relaxed as well. He has called for a rib guard as well. Does he sense uneven bounce? He would know the pitch better than anyone else.

Bang on the helmet! Mominul is down. But he straightaway gets up and says he is okay, with a thumbs up sign to follow. That is a real Day 5 pitch in the sub-continent. Kumara bangs it in short, around middle and Mominul ducks as any batsman would, under a bouncer. But then, the ball barely bounces. It shoots through and luckily for Haque, he is WATCHING THE BALL. Pretty compulsory. If he had not watched the ball, a Phillip Hughes case could have occurred. So as a normal human being's reaction would be, the reflex action takes over. Haque immediately takes his head out of the way but the ball still hits him on the rim of his helmet - the vizor. It lobs towards the slip cordon where the fielder dives and collects. No one appeals for the catch though, as everyone is concerned with Mominul's reaction.
Full and just outside off, eased through the covers for another single.
Full on middle, pushed towards the bowler once more.
Looped up, outside off, pushed towards cover.
Outside off, MH comes forward, waits for the ball to come to him and pushes it towards point.
On middle and leg, this time Haque goes back and works it towards deepish short leg.
Full and outside off, Mominul lunges and pushes it towards cover.
Some chats. Chandimal and Dilruwan have a talk and now Karunaratne comes over to give his advice too.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Ah.... slower ball, fuller in length, perhaps Das is a tad early into the shot and nearly spoons a catch back to the bowler.
Fuller, outside off, swinging in late, but Liton is upto it and drives it towards mid off.
Better ball, on a length, just outside off, coming in, no room on offer, Das defends.
Rubbish ball. On a slow track, a fast bowler is bowling in the middle of the pitch. Mominul goes back and pulls it with all the time in the world, to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Lahiru Kumara into the attack now. For the first time in this innings.
Full and down the leg side, this is swept through square leg for a run.
Outside off, pushed to point this time.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Full and outside off, pushed to cover.
On the shorter side, helped through mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, dabbed to slip.
NO BALL. Did Das hear that call? Because he was way down the track even before the ball was delivered. Was nowhere near the pitch of the ball and somehow defended it. Another crime from the bowler.

Loose shot. That ball is landed outside off and Liton goes back to cut, thinking it will turn. The ball does spin away but it is slow. The batsman is caught by surprise and ends up pushing at it. Manages to get the ball away through the covers for a single but that could have so easily been spooned to a fielder or even dragged onto the stumps.
Another long hop. Outside off, placed through the covers for one.
On the pads, but a bit too short again. Das goes back and comfortably tucks it through fine leg for a run.
Short and outside off, MH rocks back and cuts it through the covers for a single.
Landed outside off, slow loop, Haque comes forward again but does not flirt with it. Allows it to spin away into the keeper's gloves.
Full and outside off, Mominul lunges and pushes it back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, pushed towards third man but slip intervenes.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

50 FOR MOMINUL! Another fighting knock. His 13th in Tests. Can he go on to make it a big one again? That is a tad short around off, spinning in, Haque goes back and works it through square leg for three.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended by coming forward.
Outside off, pushed through point for a single.
Dilruwan Perera is back on.
Drinks!
Defended from the crease solidly.
This ball is flicked past short leg for one.
This ball is blocked towards short leg.

FOUR! Sandakan is not helping matters for his side. Drops a half-tracker on middle, Das goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Moreover, the bowler has overstepped and it is a no ball.
Driven through the covers by the batsman. They pick up a single.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Served outside off, slapped through point for a single.
Full around off, milked through to long off for a single.
Eased through mid off for a single.
Flatter around leg, Das gets down and paddles it fine. The ball rolls towards the fine leg fence but Kumara does well to save a run for his side.
The batsman has driven it through mid off. One run added to the total.
Around middle and off, whipped away through mid-wicket for one.
Haque gets to the pitch of the ball and wrists it through mid on for one. The 50-run stand between these two is up and Bangladesh are just 69 runs behind now.
The two umpires have a chat in the middle. Not sure about what. Perhaps the menu for Lunch?

FOUR! Another poor ball from Lakshan and it's duly put away. Well outside off and a touch short as well, Das goes back and slaps it through cover-point. Lots of real estate in that region and a boundary results.
Flatter on the pads, Das misses the flick and wears it on the pads.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! Liton is looking good. Sandakan needs to find his rhythm soon. He floats it up outside off on a very full length. Das gets his front foot to the pitch of the ball and drives through mid off. Perera chases it from the same position. He slides and pushes the ball back in play, but its momentum eventually takes it to the fence.
Another delivery bowled well outside off, Haque goes back and cuts it in front of square on the off side for one.
Flatter and well outside off, Das slaps it through cover-point for one.
Lakshan Sandakan is brought on now.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Haque defends this one showing the full bat face.

FOUR! Good use of the feet. Tossed up ball around off and middle, Haque gets down the track in a flash and goes across the line. Makes nice contact as the ball speed away towards deep mid-wicket. Kumara makes a mess of the diving effort there and lets it through for a boundary.
Around off and middle, pushed to mid-wicket.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Tossed up delivery outside off, Haque strides forward to defend it. The ball spins in from the rough and catches him on the front pad. A stifled appeal follows but it is turned down. Seemed to be an inside edge on the first look but replays show otherwise. Impact was well outside off and it would have gone over the stumps as well, shows Hawk Eye.
Fuller around off, driven towards covers. A maiden for Lakmal now.
Another back of a length ball on the stumps, Liton crouched low.
Banged short on the stumps, ducked under by LD.

LOW! Fuller of a good length and angling in a touch, Das stays forward to defend it on the expected bounce. The ball stays low and passes from under the bat and goes through to the keeper. Thanfully for him, the ball wasn't close to the stumps.
Fuller around off and middle, eased towards mid on for nothing.
Hurled around off and middle, defended with the full face of the bat.
Flatter on the pads, worked away off through backward square leg for one.
Rangana continues from over the wicket and lands it around middle. Liton presents a straight bat in defense.
Flatter and quicker outside off, Haque gets an outside edge as he looks to keep it out. The ball goes on the bounce to slip, who lets it through him. A single taken.
Beaten! Tossed up arm ball outside off, Mominul lunges to defend. He fails to read the straighter one and gets beaten on the outside.
Served around off, defended with a prod.
Flatter outside off, MH goes back and punches it back to the bowler.
Another short delivery on the stumps, Das ducks under that one. It goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Hurled outside off, pushed towards point to rotate strike.
Very full delivery outside off, jammed through backward point for a single.
Fuller outside off, driven straight to covers.
This one is turned through mid-wicket to rotate strike.
Lakmal comes round the wicket and hurls it full around off. Driven to mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Edged! Floated around middle, Haque gets an inside edge just past short leg for a single. It just bounced before the fielder there. The trail gets down to 89 now.
Tossed up outside off, Haque charges down and reaches out to it. Hits it straight to the man at covers.
Floated up around off, defended watchfully off the front foot.
Flatter one on the pads, Liton goes back and turns it through backward square leg for one.

FOUR! Excellently played. Herath tosses it up just outside off from round the wicket, the ball spins away just a touch. Das gets down on a knee in and flash and unfurls the sweep shot. Makes good contact with the ball and gets it in front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
Fuller than the previous delivery, Mominul goes back to defend. Ends up getting a bottom edge and the ball rolls to the off side. Decent start from Lakmal.
Suranga comes around the wicket and bangs this short slanting in. Haque crouched low to let it pass.
On a length just outside off, Liton taps it towards point and scurries to the other end. Good strategy.
Length ball, angling in. Das misses the flick and gets struck on the pads.
Similar delivery, Haque taps it towards mid-wicket. This time he sets off and completes the single as the ball didn't go straight to the fielder there.
Lakmal starts over the wicket and lands it on a length around middle and leg. Punched off the back foot towards mid-wicket.
Suranga Lakmal is brought in to bowl for the first time today.
Served around off, Das gets ahead and bunts it. A maiden from Herath.
LD gets back to the defensive mode and blocks it.
Ohh! Tossed up ball around off and middle, Das comes down the track to hit it through covers. Ends up getting it back to the bowler off the inner half.
Liton gets nicely behind this one and presents a straight bat face in defense.
Das lets it come on and just pushes it past silly point's left side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Perera bowls it on the stumps, defended towards mid-wicket.
Flighted ball around off, turned through mid-wicket for one.
Outside off, pushed through covers to get to the other end.
MH lunges and defends.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Good shot. Flatter outside off, Haque gets back and punches it through covers. Seems to have timed it pretty well to race away. But Kumara runs to his left from sweeper and fields it. There is a bit of a fumble but he keeps the batsmen down to two.
Floated around off and middle, Liton gets nicely forward and blocks.
Now Mominul rotates strike by patting it towards mid on.

SIX! Pure timing! Herath tosses it up and lands it on a fuller length, Haque gets the length that he wants. He lofts it up over the bowler's head and gets half a dozen as a result. Looking good, the southpaw.
Floated around middle, knocked down to mid on.
Defended solidly off the front foot.
Herath delivers this on a shorter length, Mominul goes back and whips it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Another delivery on the stumps, kept out with a defensive shot.
Das presses forward and bunts it.
Outside off, pushed through point for one.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball but fails.

Things happening now frequently. Tossed up outside off, Haque goes back to defends. The ball catches the outside edge and goes past slip and a couple of runs are taken. On another day and another venue for Mominul, the ball would have gone to the slip fielder.
Eased through mid on for a single.
Herath bowls an arm ball outside off, it beats the defensive bat of Mominul.

Lovely! This has spun off the rough. We saw it occasionally when Taijul was bowling it in the area wide outside off. Herath dishes it out outside off, Das looks to drive. But the ball deviates away sharply, beats the bat and goes through the gap between the slip and the keeper. Byes signaled as the batsmen run three.
Risky option! Das thinks that he has had enough of blocking the deliveries out and charges down. Ends up getting an inside edge that rolls next to the stumps on the leg side after hitting his pads.
Quicker one, Das keeps it out with a straight bat.
Floated on a fuller length, driven towards mid off.
Floated around off, Das defends it off the front foot.
Haque lunges and blocks it down.
MH has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Perera comes round the wicket and lands it around off. Haque goes back and keeps it out from the crease.
Das slinks down to this one and whips it past mid-wicket to rotate strike.
Defended solidly off the front foot onto the ground.
Floated around off from over the wicket, Das lunges forward and bunts it firmly.
Dilruwan Perera, as expected, will bowl from the other end. A slip and a short leg are the close in fielders for him.
This is delivered on a flatter trajectory outside off, Das transfers his weight on the back foot and punches it past silly point for a run to get off the mark straightaway.

We are all set to get underway. Liton Das is the new batsman walking in as Mushfiqur Rahim was dismissed in what turned out to be the last ball of the day. He will face Rangana Herath, who has one delivery left in the over. A slip, gully and a silly point in place. Mominul Haque stands at the other end.

Mehidy Hasan is up for a chat and he reckons that Mominul Haque, Liton Das, Mahmudullah apart from him are yet to bat and he seems confident of doing well. Adds that they will look to do their best. Reckons that some deliveries are turning square while some go on straight and that makes it tough for batting. Ends hoping to fare well with the bat on the pitch that has just spiced up.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo is out there inspecting the track on this final day. He stands at the Rocket end and reckons that the Sri Lankan spinners would be licking their lips. The track is dry at that end and he expects them to get a lot of assistance from here. He adds further that there are enough roughs at the other end and hence, he isn't going closer to have a look there. Ends saying that smothering the spin by using the feet is the key.

Sri Lanka have played like one of those sides, who create a mirage of playing the catch-up game for most times, only to slip ahead and boss the game. Their three main spinners have picked up a wicket apiece and these are good signs for them. They have a week of wickets to be snaffled up. Dinesh Chandimal and Co. would look to go all out and quell any semblance of fightback that would be on display from the home side. Is this the final script or do we have another twist in the offing? Stay with us as we sail through Day 5.

Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium and Mominul Haque is a love story. The southpaw averages over 85 at the venue and his 176 in the first essay stood testimony to that. Looking at the way Bangladesh played in the first innings, it was hard to imagine that they would find themselves in a quagmire that they are in now. They are staring at a 119-run deficit and an innings defeat looms. The Chittagong Hero is still in the middle for them, though. Can he further his romance with the ground with a rescue act for his side? On this backdrop, we take pleasure in having your company with us for the final day in this first Test between Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
... Final Day, First Session ...

A final day finish beckons. The track is suddenly not a placid one. The catches are suddenly going straight to the fielders. These are all dangerous pointers for Bangladesh. They need to bat well to escape with a draw here. Didn't imagine myself writing anything close to this till the previous session. Sri Lanka would turn up refreshed and hungry for more. We'll love to have you all tomorrow. Do join us at 0930 local time (0330 GMT) for all the action. Cheers! Adios! Take care! To enjoy some crisp T20I cricket, you may switch tabs for the Australia vs New Zealand game.

Earlier in the day, the tourists played an attritional brand of cricket to keep the hosts on the field for 1197 balls. At a point it felt as if the lucid surface had made them resign to the fact that it was futile to expose their bowlers to this surface. No great urgency to score was shown. However, they crawled their way forward to a mammoth score, which means the hosts are still 119 runs behind. Roshen Silva went past the triple figure mark while Dinesh Chandimal and Niroshan Dickwella failed to get theirs. For the hosts, Taijul Islam picked up a four-fer. Looking back now, one can understand and laud the Lankans' strategy with the bat.

Dramatic end to an otherwise staid day! Sri Lanka have wrested back the initiative in a big time here. After thinking that 200 runs are enough in their bank, they came out, armed with experienced and incisive spinners, on the field. The home side openers kept them at bay for 90 balls and 52 runs. But that opening was enough for the visitors to make further inroads, sending a couple more back in the hut. It should be made clear, however, that there is nothing on the surface to suggest that it is unplayable, as the wickets to fall have been because of the batters' undoing.

OUT! What a moment in the game! The analogue clock on the ground showed local time to be 1630 yet the umpires went by the watch that they had in their hands, which meant that another over was squeezed in. And lo, the hosts lose one of the mainstays in what turns out to be the last delivery of the day. What's more, Chandimal brought Herath on to bowl this one and his move has paid off big time. The veteran tosses this one around off, Rahim gets a big stride forward to defend. The ball takes the inside edge, hits the front pad, lobs off the boot and Mendis takes a stunner at silly point. The Lankans are confidently ecstatic as they feel they have got their man. However, the dreaded finger from the umpire is not raised. Rod Tucker goes to his partner, has a longish chat with Marais Erasmus and takes it upstairs, giving the soft signal as Not Out. Time for another look, which seals the deal. It shows that the ball has hit the pad after taking the inside edge, lobbed off the boot and is in the air a bit. The man from silly point has taken a clean catch as well, concludes the TV umpire. Thus the on-field call is overturned and that means, Rahim has to walk back to the pavilion, this time 98 runs short of a ton. Also, that's STUMPS ON THE PENULTIMATE DAY!

What's happened here? There is a catch taken at silly point, the Lankans go up in unison for that. They seem very confident with this. Rod Tucker confers with the leg umpire and takes it upstairs. The soft signal is NOT OUT.
Bunted off the front foot onto the ground.
Outside off, driven through covers for one.
This one is played to mid-wicket off the inner half.
Floated around off, Haque goes back and defends it to the on side.
Hello! We have time for another over, feel the umpires and here we go... Rangana Herath to bowl the final one. He started this innings and now will end the day.
Sandakan comes over the wicket and flights it full on middle and leg. Rahim bunts it solidly.
Should be the last ball for the day. Rahim does some gardening and then gets ready to face it...
Tossed up around off, Rahim bunts it off the front foot.
Fuller in length, hit to mid-wicket.
Rahim goes back and sees this off with a straight bat.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Leg slip in place now.
Floated well outside off, Rahim strides forward and blocks it to short leg.
Last over of the day coming up. Rahim is taking his time to ensure that it is the last one for sure. He is signaling to the dressing room to get him some tablets. Not sure what for.
Pushed defensively through covers to retain strike.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This is quicker and fuller on the stumps. Rahim gets back quickly and defends it to short leg.
Tossed up outside off and drops it on a fuller length. Rahim gets behind the line nicely and smothers it.
Floated outside off, Rahim lets it spin in and defends it to the off side.
Dropped on a length that is on the shorter side, Mominul goes back quickly and punches it through covers to rotate strike.
Rahim goes back and defends it with a straight bat.
Swept away to the man at square leg.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Tossed up around off, Haque pushes it towards covers. Perera gets to his left from point, slides. But he is unable to prevent the single.
This is the googly, Rahim reads it well and plays it towards the off side. Quickly gets to the other end to open his account.
Tossed up around off, Rahim lunges forward and keeps it out.
Flighted delivery around off, bunted.
Flatter on the pads, worked away towards square leg.
Leg slip comes to silly point now.
Defended off the front foot onto the ground.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.

Sri Lanka are now showing what their spinners are capable of. Perera floats it just around off, forcing Mominul to lunge forward in defense. But the ball spins away just enough to beat the outside edge. It wasn't far from the off pole as well. Dickwella failed to collect that.
Shortish in length, cut away to point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated around off and middle, eased to mid on.
Mushfiqur Rahman makes his way out to the center. He missed out getting to triple figures in the first innings and should look to rectify the same this time around.

OUT! Delight for Sandakan, despair for Tamim! Nicely tossed up outside off, Iqbal lunges forward to defend. Stretches out to reach the ball and all he does is gets a thick outside edge to the keeper. Dickwella pouches it to his left and sets off the celebrations for the Sri Lankans. Haque from the other end, asks Tamim to take the review but the latter replies that he had indeed edged it. The hosts rocked back early in the second innings.
Shortish delivery outside off, punched to covers.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated outside off on a shortish length, Haque goes back and pulls it to mid on. He scurries to the other end, beating the wild shy from the fielder.
Lakshan Sandakan introduced into the attack.
Another one in line of the stumps, defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Flatter and shorter outside off, Tamim goes back and cuts it fiercely through point for a boundary.
Landed outside off, Iqbal strides forward but gets beaten by the away turn on that.
TI gets behind that solidly and keeps it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Poor delivery, punished. De Silva dishes out a low full toss outside off, Haque makes full use of that. Mominul drives it powerfully through covers for a boundary. Silly point had to take evasive action, which he did with a jump.
Kept out from the crease.
Looped up around off and middle, Mominul strides to defend.
Haque goes back to this one and bunts it from the crease.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted delivery around middle and leg, flicked away through mid-wicket for a brace.
The batsman plays the Square-Cut.
Turned away off the pads for a single through square leg.
Haque looks to defend but gets a soft outside edge towards slip.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Eased through mid on to rotate strike.
Flatter outside off, cut away for a single.
TI stands back and defends.
Defended from the crease.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

MADE IT! Iqbal strides forward to defend but the ball takes the inside edge and it rolls to the on side in front of square. The man from square leg, Mendis, one thinks, gets there and strikes the bull's eye at the bowler's end. Although Tamim seems in, it is taken upstairs. Replays find him easily in.
Direct hit at the bowler's end! Tamim Iqbal seems to be in there, but the umpire takes it upstairs, just to be safe.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller on off, driven towards mid off.
This ball is nudged off his pads through square leg for a brace.
Haque drives it straight to the man at covers.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
MH lunges forward and defends that watchfully.
Fired in line of the stumps, defended off the back foot.
Served outside off, punched through covers for two.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up around middle and leg, flicked away round the corner for one.
Haque fails to sweep this one and gets hit on the pads.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fuller outside off, driven through covers for one.
Flatter delivery, worked away off the pads for a brace.
Mominul Haque makes way to the middle next. Remember, he stroked a splendid 176 in the first essay. His side needs a similar innings here.

OUT! Atrocious, irresponsible, reckless - call it whatever you want. The end result is, Bangladesh lose their first. Floated up in line of the stumps, Kayes gets down to scoop it fine. Ends up getting a bottom edge to that and the ball lobs to backward square leg for the simplest of catches, which Chandimal doesn't falter taking. The 52-run stand is done and dusted. Hard to understand that shot when your team is looking to see the day off. The hosts are still 148 behind.
Worked through backward square leg to rotate strike.
Floated delivery around off, beaten yet again due to the away turn.

Confusion! That's the last thing the hosts require. Tamim works this ball towards square leg. Dickwella rushes quickly to the ball. The batter was down in search of the single, a yes-no call from his partner made him wait there. Eventually he returns into the crease safely.
Flatter on middle and leg, worked away through backward square leg for one.

Lovely! Tossed up delivery that lands on off. Kayes lunges forward to defend but the ball spins away past the outside edge and goes to the keeper. A ball here and there that spins like this, is enough to create doubts in the minds of the batsmen.
Last drinks break for the day!
Floated outside off, punched through covers for one. That raises the fifty for Bangladesh.
Straighter one around off, Kayes lets it come on before defending. The ball takes an inside edge onto his pads.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Slashes and slashes hard! Sri Lanka won't mind this. Tossed up ball outside off, Imrul gets down on a knee and looks to go over covers. Ends up getting a thick outside edge over the slip fielder and the ball races away to the fence.
Kayes gets forward and defends.
Pushed outside off, driven through covers. They take a quick single. There is a wild throw at the bowler's end, the ball goes towards sweeper. No extra run results though.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Around middle and leg, flicked away off the pads, straight to short leg.
Quicker one on a length just around off, Tamim goes back and punches it past silly point for one.
Silly point in place.
Served around off and middle, defended solidly off the front foot.

FOUR! Tamim's intentions are crystal clear. Sees this tossed up ball on the stumps, he slinks down the track and looks to go over the top. Gets it off the inner half but has enough to clear mid on with ease.
Begins with a flighted ball fuller in length, driven straight to mid on.
Dilruwan Perera is into the attack now.
Tossed up delivery on the stumps, kept out with a forward defense.
Lunged forward and blocked off the front foot.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
De Silva lands it around off, Imrul looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Flatter on off and middle, defended.
Tossed up around middle and leg, Iqbal gets down the track to block. Gets an inside edge past short leg for one.
Gives it nice loop, Kayes presses forward and blocks.
Kayes punched the ball off the back foot.
Quicker on the stumps, punched down to long on for a single.
Very full on the stumps, Iqbal jams it out.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Presses forward and defends.

LBW appeal but maybe, there was an inside edge! Fuller and straighter on the stumps, Tamim prods forward to defend but seems to have gotten an inside edge and then gets hit on the pads. De Silva keeps appealing and now the whole of the Lankan team joins. The umpire shakes his head. Replays spots an inside edge.
Attempted off break which doesn't spin and stays really low. Iqbal leans forward and manages to keep it out.
Loopy ball outside off, driven a bit uppishly towards Herath at deepish mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Hangs back and shows a straight bat.
Floated delivery around middle and leg, worked away towards short mid-wicket.
Dhananjaya de Silva is brought into the attack.
FOUR! With the spin! Tossed up delivery outside off, Tamim gets down and nails the sweep through square leg for a boundary. off the meet it came!
Iqbal covers the line and keeps it out.
Eased down to mid on for a single.
Around middle and leg, nudged towards the man at mid on.
IK dances down the track but decides to defend it.
Tossed up delivery outside off, Imrul drives it towards mid off.
Sprays down the leg side, Iqbal moves inside the line to let it be. A maiden for Lakmal!
Drifting in on the pads, Kayes works it away through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Drags his length short, Kayes bends down to evade it.

A loud, loud shout for an LBW! Umpire Erasmus stays put. Lakmal fires in a yorker on the stumps, Kayes looks to jam it out and seems to have gotten an inside edge before getting hit on the pads. Suranga keeps appealing but gets no attention. Chandimal walks to him has a word but they decide not to take the DRS. Snicko spots a clear inside edge.
Length delivery, angling in on middle and leg, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
Darts in a fuller ball on off, Imrul looks to jam it out but fails to get any wood on it.

SIX! Down the track and Kayes goes bang! What a hit! All this while he was kept quiet by Herath. This time he sees the flight, decides to wear the dancing shoes on and smacks it high and handsome over the bowler's head for a maximum.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Slower through the air, landed full outside off, Kayes prods forward in defense.
Flatter delivery around middle and off, Imrul hangs back in defense.
Tossed up delivery outside off, blocked off the front foot.
Length delivery, angling in on middle and leg, worked towards the square leg fielder.
Short of a length delivery on middle, Tamim hops and tucks it away towards the square leg fielder.
Good length delivery on off, Tamim looks to drive it away but squirts it off the inner half to square leg.
Another short ball but the line is not the one that will threaten the batsman. Tamim once again ducks but Lakmal will have to reload as he overstepped.
Bangs in a short one, it kicks off the deck. Tamim is quick to sit under it.
Slightly fuller, just outside off, Iqbal leans forward and keeps it out towards cover.
On a good length and angling in on middle, defended back to the bowler who, in his followthrough, collects it with his right hand and mimes a throw at Tamim.
Kayes presses forward and kills it back down the turf.
Quicker through the air outside off, Imrul Kayes goes for the reverse sweep but fails to get going with the shot. Trying to give Herath a dose of his own medicine?
Tamim milks a single down to long on.
Quicker and flatter outside off, slapped hard but finds the man at point.
Tossed up on the stumps, wristed away to mid on.
Tossed up on off, driven through the cover region for a single.
FOUR! Easy for Tamim! Lakmal delivers it on a fuller length but sprays it on the pads, Tamim wrists it along the carpet in front of square on the leg side. Races away! Good start for Bangladesh!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Eases this full ball straight to mid off.
Lakmal once again keeps it full and it's on the pads, Tamim leans across and flicks it through the gap at mid-wicket again. Comes back for a couple.
Fuller in length and angling in, clipped through mid-wicket for one.
Good length on off, defended off the back foot to the bowler.
Tamim leans forward to defend but this one goes straight on with the arm. Beats the outside edge as Dickwella whips the bails off. Iqbal's back foot was grounded though.
FOUR! Good shot! Loopy delivery around middle and leg, Tamim flicks it neatly through the gap at mid-wicket to pick up a boundary.
Loopy ball around middle, flicked towards short mid-wicket.
Worked away through mid on for a single.
Tossed up ball outside off, IK comes down the track and pushes it to the fielder at cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Beaten! On a length and shaping away just a touch, Iqbal has a tentative poke inside the line but it misses the outside edge by a whisker.
On a length and outside off, Tamim keeps his bat inside the line to leave it alone.
Fuller in length and outside off, Tamim drives it through mid off and comes back for a brace.
On a good length and in the channel outside off, Tamim shoulders his arms to it.
FOUR! Superb! Back of a length delivery, but the line is wider outside off, Iqbal cracks it through cover. Away she races to the fence for a boundary.
Good length delivery, slanting away outside off, Iqbal defended off the back foot.
Suranga Lakmal to share the new cherry from the other end.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. Tidy stuff from Herath!
Loopy delivery outside off, driven towards the cover fielder.
Tossed up on off, worked towards mid on.
Bangladesh are away and so is Tamim! Floated delivery around leg, flicked towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Bowls it a bit too full, Iqbal brings his bat down and wrists it towards mid on.
Starts off from over the wicket and lands it around middle, Tamim prods forward and works it towards the short leg fielder.
